To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the magnetic axes and the axial ligand orientations of the oxidized cytochromes from Geobacter spp. are conserved.

the magnetic axes of the heme groups of PpcA are defined by the orientation of the axial histidines and the magnetic properties (anisotropy of the g-tensor and zero-field splitting parameter) of the hemes.

we have determined the geometry of the axial ligands, the magnetic properties of all the hemes and the orientation of the hemes of the periplasmic cytochrome PccA from Geobactor metallireducens using paramagnetic NMR spectroscopy.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the structural, functional and magnetic properties of cytochromes from Geobacter species, with the aim of contributing to the understanding of the electron transfer mechanisms in these bacteria.

the study of the magnetic properties of heme proteins, and their application to the structural characterization of proteins, in particular, the determination of the orientations of the axial ligands of heme groups.
the study of the structural and functional properties of periplasmic cytochromes from Geobacter bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heme magnetic axes of PccA from Geobactor sulfurreducens are parallel to the heme planes, with the hemes 2 and 3 having a more axial character than the heme 1.
the magnetic axes of the three hemes in the oxidized state of PpcA are oriented in the order H1 > H2 > H3, and the axial histidine ligands of H1 and H2 are oriented in the same direction.

this study is a contribution to the knowledge of the structure-function relationship in the cytochromes from Geobacter bacteria, which are important for bioremediation processes and bioelectrochemical applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to determine the orientation of the hemes and the axial histidines for PpcA from the metal reducing bacterium Geobacter metalli-reducens.
the use of paramagnetic NMR to determine the orientation of the hemes and the geometry of their axial ligands is a powerful tool for the study of c-type cytochromes.

the magnetic properties of PpcA are similar to those previously determined for the homolog cytochrome PccA from Geobater sulfurreducens, and that the magnetic axes of these two cytochromes are very close to the same orientation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
13C Nuclei-Relaxation Dispersion NMR experiments can be used to determine the geometry of the axial ligands and the magnetic axes of the hemes of triheme proteins.
paramagnetic NMR can be successfully used to determine the orientation of the hemes and the magnetic axes in cytochromes.
the magnetic properties of PpcA are conserved between G. metallireduccens and G. sulfurreducens, which suggests that these magnetic properties may be important for the function of the protein.
